subject: english
question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Hardly had __we get in but__ the train started.
solution:
The correct answer is** option 2.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the** past tense.**
 
• So we need to use the past tense form of the verb "**get**" which is "**got**"
 
• There are two clauses in the sentence which are linked by a conjunction.
 
• The use of the conjunction **"but" **is incorrect here.
 
• There are two events happening at the same time or very close to each other.
 
• We need to use the subordinate conjunction **"when" **
 
• The subordinate conjunction **when **is used to **denote time** in a sentence,
 
• **When **is used to talk about events that took place in the **past**.
 
• In the given sentence, the speaker wants to say they had hardly entered the train when the train started moving.

**The correct sentence is**: *Hardly had we got in when__ the train started.*

Hence, the correct sentence is **option 2.**
